beats.say: A single line of binary search — low plus high divided by two — survived in production libraries for twenty years. Plot every valid thirty-two-bit pair of low and high on a plane. Your unit tests sit in one tiny safe corner, while half of all valid inputs overflow and fail.

Testing checks the points you thought to write. Formal verification checks the entire space. An SMT solver like Z3 proves the overflow mathematically in milliseconds. TLA+ model checking exhaustively explores distributed protocol states. Proof assistants like Lean 4 verify theorems over infinitely many inputs.

When AI generates thousands of lines of code, human code review becomes the bottleneck. Formal verification flips the game: the proof checker does not care who wrote the code or the proof — only that every logical step holds. Next in the series: watching TLA+ hunt down a five-step distributed bug.
